WFR-01.description: bundle_id and review_content_id are distinct, independently computed, and independently testable

WFR-02.description: wrapper-only bundle changes produce a new bundle_id but an unchanged review_content_id

WFR-03.description: external feedback is matched against bundle_id exactly; stale/missing feedback is rejected naming both values

WFR-04.description: approval records store both reviewed_bundle_id and approved_review_content_id; only the latter gates future durability

WFR-05.description: the native-git manifest represents additions, modifications, deletions, renames, mode changes, symlinks, binaries, and unusual-but-supported paths deterministically; unsupported cases fail closed

WFR-06.description: the committed plan exactly matches the reviewed working-tree content after the plan-approval commit

WFR-07.description: commit-trailer lookup is exact, full-identifier, work-item-scoped, ancestry-limited, requires exactly one match, with a stated tie-break for legitimate duplicates

WFR-08.description: approval freshness is checked against current committed content, per stage, with no basis branch

WFR-09.description: WORKFLOW_CONFIG.json's repository-level default is separate from any work item's governing_workflow_version; missing/corrupt config fails safe to "1" only pre-activation

WFR-10.description: WF-Activate changes only the repository-level default and records activation in a durable commit trailer; rollback is an equally durable trailer event

WFR-11.description: the manual dry run exercises real v2.1 command behavior via an isolated synthetic work item, with its active-pointer save/restore persisted across intended session boundaries

WFR-12.description: a failed or interrupted dry run has a defined, user-approved rollback and resumption path that does not retroactively affect items created under "2.1"

WFR-13.description: immutable requirement mapping lives in a separate machine-readable file from the mutable execution ledger

WFR-14.description: checkpoint status/start-commit exist in exactly one writable place (WORKFLOW_STATE.json's checkpoints[id]); the registry carries no status column

WFR-15.description: WF-M8a/WF-M8b and WF4c depend on the checkpoints that build the schema/writer they use

WFR-16.description: source proposal files are excluded from normal review bundles

WFR-17.description: the bundle records its generation worktree_root and HEAD as diagnostic metadata; local commands (not external reviewers) stop if their own worktree/HEAD differs

WFR-18.description: WORKFLOW_STATE.json is genuinely multi-item: Milestone 8's dormant legacy entry and the active work item coexist and resolve independently by ID

WFR-19.description: neither new approval gate's entry condition reads the approval record its own exit action writes

WFR-20.description: no gate requires a clean tree that tracked workflow state itself makes unreachable

WFR-21.description: plan_approval durability survives checkpoint commits; recomputation is scoped per stage; no field attempts to store its own containing commit

WFR-22.description: reviewed_implementation_head has exactly one writer (the bundle generator, implementation/post-fix stage)

WFR-23.description: the checkpoint-selection algorithm is deterministic across independent fresh sessions

WFR-24.description: user-only enforcement of /approve-review and /accept-milestone relies only on named, supported controls (disable-model-invocation plus explicit confirmation-text validation)

WFR-25.description: the checkpoint registry and requirement mapping are tracked, machine-readable JSON files; the Markdown views are generated and never hashed directly

WFR-26.description: every command this milestone modifies appears in the dual-mode enumeration, including /milestone-plan, /apply-plan-review, /apply-implementation-review

WFR-27.description: the .ai-review/<work_item_id>/ relayout has a stated migration covering this milestone's own in-flight bundle

WFR-28.description: docs/TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md carries the fingerprint toolchain decision; CI runs the hermetic conformance suite on every PR

WFR-29.description: supported_versions gates work-item creation; waived_guarantees and work_item_kind are validated enums

WFR-30.description: WORKTREE_IDENTITY.json has a named writer and refresh point

WFR-31.description: every tracked WORKFLOW_STATE.json field has at least one documented reader

WFR-32.description: a one-time bootstrap path commits the already-reviewed prototype/CI/decision artifacts and the bootstrap continuation command under Workflow v1, without touching docs/ACTIVE_MILESTONE.md or docs/ROADMAP.md

WFR-33.description: the bootstrap continuation command implements exactly one checkpoint per invocation and never loops, so no session relies on command text it edited earlier in that same session

WFR-34.description: a dormant Milestone-8 legacy item transitions to an active v2.1-governed item only via an explicit, user-invoked adoption step (a work-item-id selector argument on /prepare-functional-review) that consumes the imported technical approval and never runs implicitly

WFR-35.description: broad functional remediation has an explicit child-work-item identity and its own approval lifecycle, without mutating the original completed checkpoint registry

WFR-36.description: WF8a-i's fixture harness scaffolding is itself verifiable: a documented fixture format that WF8a-ii's cross-checkpoint tests consume

WFR-37.description: /review-plan implements the local-plan-review role independent of any specific Claude model, in role-oriented (not model-named) state/schema terms, and refuses cleanly outside a "2.1"-governed work item at the correct phase

WFR-38.description: for a "2.1" item, plan approval is unreachable without both plan-review stages recorded in order against the same review_content_id; any accepted plan edit invalidates both stages and returns to AWAITING_LOCAL_PLAN_REVIEW, never self-declared ready by /apply-plan-review

WFR-39.description: the exact bundle path, bundle_id, and review_content_id handed to the manual external reviewer are displayed by /review-plan; a wrapper-only bundle regeneration after local approval does not invalidate the completed local-review stage

WFR-40.description: the concise plan-review operator guide (docs/ai-workflow/PLAN_REVIEW_WORKFLOW.md) is an excluded (not protected) plan-stage artifact, authored against the commands WF4a-iv actually builds, so its creation never stales a plan approval

WFR-41.description: each of the six local/manual verdict x entry-state cells in the plan-review transition table has a named sole writer, a named destination (or explicit non-transition for BLOCK), and stated validation preconditions; a local REVISE can never enter AWAITING_MANUAL_EXTERNAL_PLAN_REVIEW; /record-manual-plan-review is the sole writer of the manual-stage ledger and refuses stale, wrong-role, wrong-work-item, wrong-phase, or duplicate ingestion

WFR-42.description: every path in PLAN_STAGE_PROTECTED is present in the working tree at bundle-generation time; plan-stage computation fails closed, naming the path, if one is absent

WFR-43.description: WF0 refuses to create its commit unless the approving feedback carries Reviewed bundle ID:/Reviewed base commit:/Work item:, each matching the bundle it approved; WF0 refuses feedback declaring a "2.1"-only reviewer role for this permanently-"1" work item

WFR-44.description: manual-ingestion validation is review_content_id-equality-hard, bundle_id-equality-advisory; the ledger records the feedback's actual bundle_id in both cases

WFR-45.description: plan-stage classification covers every path any concurrent operation (not only this work item's own checkpoints) may write; a path this work item's plan declares out of scope is explicitly excluded, never merely unmentioned

WFR-46.description: MANIFEST.md writing is read-only by default and requires an explicit separately-named invocation; both bundle_id and review_content_id are computed last and asserted idempotent before the manifest is considered final; plan_revision is sourced from the registry JSON, not a caller-supplied literal, and cross-checked against the plan document's declared revision; REVIEW_REQUEST.md states review_content_id and bundle generation asserts it agrees with MANIFEST.md
